conflict_topics: ventilation responsibility / standing rule for cooks
opening window vs. protecting drying laundry
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents use short, context-appropriate statements and physical actions (turning extractor on, releasing/taking stove) which ground the dialogue.
Agent A explicitly refused a standing rule early and never retracted; others negotiated a practical workaround instead.
Agent C introduced a concrete condition (ask before opening window) linking a factual constraint (drying rack) to policy.
Few needless repetitions; most turns advanced either action or clarified conditions.
evaluation.final_reason: Immediate practical issues were addressed: extractor left on, stove access handled, and others agreed to ask before opening the window so laundry is protected. However, the substantive normative dispute about whether cooks must accept a standing rule assigning them ventilation responsibility was not accepted by Agent A and was not resolved by the end of the transcript, leaving a partial resolution.
position_change_notes: Agent A retained their position of rejecting a standing rule assigning ventilation responsibility; they did, however, take immediate practical action (turned extractor on) and freed the stove.
Agent B consistently advocated for cooks to ventilate and proposed a standing rule; B moved toward deferring formal adoption ('we can talk later') while securing practical compliance.
Agent C maintained a protective stance toward their drying laundry and secured an explicit condition (be asked before window opening); this position was adopted by others.
Agent D accepted the practical norms (keep extractor on, ask before opening window) when they began cooking, aligning with B and C on practice though not explicitly addressing A's earlier refusal.

round_scores.evidence: Agent B demanded immediate ventilation and a standing rule that cooks ventilate; Agent A explicitly refused to accept a standing rule and refused to shift responsibility but turned the extractor on. Stove-release demand from Agent D was present but not yet acted on. Practical smell mitigation began (extractor on) while the normative dispute over a rule remained unresolved.

Agent B asked Agent A to leave extractor on for five more minutes and suggested discussing a rule later; Agent A removed the dish and physically released the stove. The immediate access conflict over the stove was resolved, but the standing-rule dispute about who must ventilate remained unsettled.

Agent C requested that no one open the window while their drying rack is present and asked to be consulted if the window must be opened; Agent D agreed to keep the extractor on and to ask before opening. The laundry/window concern was asserted and others accommodated, reducing but not eliminating the underlying ventilation-rule disagreement.

Agent B proposed a simple standing rule (cooks turn extractor on); Agent C accepted that rule conditionally (do not open the window while my rack is there—ask first). Agent A did not accept the proposed standing rule (earlier refused it and did not retract that refusal), so the normative dispute about a formal rule remained, though practice was aligning among others.

Agent D took the stove and committed to keep the extractor on and to ask Agent C before opening the window. Practical arrangements for ventilation and window-consultation were in place among B, C, and D; Agent A's earlier explicit refusal to accept a standing rule was not overturned, leaving a minor unresolved normative disagreement.

No new statements. Confirmed state shows extractor on, window closed, Agent D cooking. The operational conflict (odor, stove access, window) is largely managed in practice, but the standing-rule question originally opposed by Agent A remains unaddressed by Agent A, so a minor substantive disagreement persists.

substantive_insights: Practical accommodation (use extractor, ask before opening window) can defuse an immediate resource conflict even if parties disagree about a formal rule.

There is a trade-off between odor ventilation and protecting drying laundry; the group resolved this by delegating immediate ventilation to the extractor and requiring consent before opening the window.
Stove access conflict was brief and resolved by the cook freeing the stove once the dish was done, showing temporal coordination can remove some tensions.
